scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP.statement: Dispute ticket surge is driven by inadequate response/triage capacity in Customer Service, not by bills actually being wrong; automating responses would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules (e.g. estimate-substitution logic) around August introduced systematic wrong bills, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-EXPORT-DEGRADATION.statement: AMI read delivery from the vendor (MDMS nightly export) degraded or failed more often starting around August, pushing more accounts into estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Manual field meter-reading completion dropped or became unreliable, increasing estimated bills that customers then dispute.

H-SEASONAL-USAGE-MISPERCEPTION.statement: Bills are correct but reflect a legitimate seasonal consumption increase; the 'dispute surge' is customer pushback on accurate higher bills rather than billing errors.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A field-reader staffing shortfall (3 readers short) since July is the specific cause of late manual-read routes feeding H-FIELD-READ-GAP, as claimed by SH-FIELD.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION-R.statement: A billing import validation threshold rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing those accounts into estimate substitution and producing wrong bills for the majority of disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts.

H-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT.statement: BV-17 compares raw register value against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none (E-12); this possible unit-mismatch defect could misclassify consumption as anomalously high for both ESTIMATED (via rejection to substitution, E-11) and ACTUAL (via miscalculated bill amount) read types.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM response-time data (2440 tickets) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day SLA, indicating Customer Service is currently meeting its response-time target rather than falling behind on triage/response capacity.

Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 manual-read accounts. This is a measurable manual-read completion shortfall that would push some unread accounts into estimate substitution, a candidate (but not yet quantified) driver of the dispute surge.

CRM monthly ticket counts (610 Jun, 590 Jul, 1180 Aug, 1260 Sep) show volume roughly flat through July then almost exactly doubling in August and staying elevated/rising in September. This confirms the timing and magnitude of the surge CL-01 describes, but says nothing about why bills are wrong or disputes are rising — it is a symptom measurement, not a cause.

The tariff change log shows zero recorded tariff/rate changes, ruling out a rate change as the source of the wrong-bill/dispute surge; it does not speak to read delivery, estimate-substitution rules, field reading, or response capacity.

Billing-db shows 3025 disputed bills split by read type: 1785 tied to ACTUAL reads and 1240 to ESTIMATED reads, so disputes are not concentrated on estimated/substituted bills. This weakens read-gap and AMI-degradation explanations as the dominant driver and points toward a billing-side issue affecting both read types.

E-05 still shows disputed bills split 1785 ACTUAL vs 1240 ESTIMATED (billing-db, F-05) — the raw observation is unchanged. It no longer supports a single read-type-agnostic billing import rule defect: E-11 shows the only identified concrete mechanism (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejection to estimate substitution) structurally applies only to the ESTIMATED population, giving no mechanism for the 1785 ACTUAL-type disputes, so the balanced split can no longer be read as evidence of one rule change hitting both read types.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's unverified statement that there has been no tariff change this year echoes the same claim already established authoritatively by E-04 (tariff_change_log, 0 records). It adds no new decision-relevant information beyond what the tool evidence already shows.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortfall of three readers since July has caused manual-read routes to run late, pushing those customers onto estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder explanation for the route-completion shortfall already measured in E-02; it offers a mechanism but does not address why E-05 shows disputes split roughly evenly across actual and estimated read types.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document confirms the contractual basis for K-DISPATCH: route priority changes (push_route_update) may be requested by the utility but are executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation. It settles who holds approval authority over the field-dispatch protected action but says nothing about the cause of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) returns per-route completion detail for 14 routes, sample R-00 at 0.70 completion. This gives route-level granularity underlying the aggregate 88% completion already seen in E-02, but it reports completion only — it is not yet cross-referenced with dispute-ticket counts per route, so it does not by itself establish how much of the dispute surge the route shortfall explains.

E-10.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder message) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned per vendor ticket TX-4471, meaning the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query may now be executable. This is an unverified claim of a status change, not a confirmed tool/system state, and says nothing about the dispute surge's cause.

MDMS export records for disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts show 1184 of 1240 had an AMI read received before cutoff but rejected at billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (despite being exported to billing), while only 56 had no read received at all. This identifies a specific billing-import rejection mechanism that forces valid high-consumption AMI reads into estimate substitution, pointing to a billing-side validation defect rather than AMI delivery failure or field-read gaps for this account population.

E-12.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The billing-config change log (E-12) shows rule BV-17 — a "high-consumption check" comparing raw register value against 12-month m3 history, with unit_scaling=none — was deployed 2026-08-01, exactly matching the dispute surge onset (E-03). This directly confirms a billing import validation rule change occurred near August 2026 and names the rule behind E-11's REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION status; the other entry (BV-09, a label-text change on 2026-03-02) is unrelated to the surge timing.

This weakens read-gap and AMI-degradation explanations as the dominant driver and points toward a billing-side issue affecting both read types.
ER-1.revised_interpretation: E-05 still shows disputed bills split 1785 ACTUAL vs 1240 ESTIMATED (billing-db, F-05) — the raw observation is unchanged. U-RULE-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.question: Did the billing import validation rules (DA-RULES / billing-config log) actually change around August 2026, and if so what specifically changed (e.g. estimate-substitution logic)?
U-RULE-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.decision_impact: If no rule change is found, H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE is falsified and the root_problem's causal mechanism must be revisited before any bill-correction action is designed.
U-RULE-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.resolution_path: Query billing-config (DA-RULES) change-log entries near Jul-Aug 2026 and compare dates to the dispute surge onset (F-03), per SC-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.
U-RULE-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.safe_placeholder: Proceed with diagnostic correlation only; do not draft any bill correction plan or write adjustments until the rule-change event is confirmed in DA-RULES.
U-RULE-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.resolution: E-11 identifies the candidate mechanism (a REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION import rule discarding valid AMI reads) answering 'what specifically changed', but does not come from billing-config/DA-RULES and so does not confirm the August timing of the rule; DA-RULES change-log confirmation is still required before this unknown can be closed.

U-FIELD-ROUTE-CONTRIBUTION.question: How much, if any, of the dispute surge is independently attributable to the manual-read route completion shortfall (E-02), despite the balanced ACTUAL/ESTIMATED split in E-05?
U-FIELD-ROUTE-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether field-route remediation should be pursued in parallel with the billing-rule fix or deprioritized as a minor secondary factor.
U-FIELD-ROUTE-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Cross-reference the route-log completion shortfall (E-02) against disputed-ticket accounts to quantify any independent contribution.
U-FIELD-ROUTE-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Treat the field-route shortfall as a secondary, unquantified contributing factor, not the primary driver, pending this analysis.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-BLOCKED.question: Can AMI read-event data (DA-MDMS) be reviewed at all, given the vendor export access is on HOLD (ACCESS_PENDING, recovery_decision seq 72)?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-BLOCKED.decision_impact: Blocks fully ruling AMI/MDMS degradation in or out as a contributing cause until vendor access is restored; low impact since E-05 already weighs against that hypothesis.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-BLOCKED.resolution_path: Await vendor provisioning of MDMS export access before any AMI read-event analysis is attempted.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-BLOCKED.safe_placeholder: Exclude AMI/MDMS read-event data from the diagnostic scope and rely only on billing-db, route-log and billing-config evidence.

U-SEASONAL-CONFOUND.question: Could part of the dispute volume increase reflect legitimate seasonal consumption increases (H-SEASONAL-USAGE-MISPERCEPTION) rather than billing errors, confounding the dispute-volume-back-to-baseline success metric?
U-SEASONAL-CONFOUND.decision_impact: Affects whether the dispute-volume-recovery success criterion (<=~600/month) is an achievable/appropriate sole success measure or needs a seasonally-adjusted baseline.
U-SEASONAL-CONFOUND.resolution_path: Compare year-over-year seasonal consumption patterns against the Aug-Sep dispute spike to rule in or out a seasonal confound.
U-SEASONAL-CONFOUND.safe_placeholder: Treat full recovery to ~600/month as a provisional target pending this check, not as the only valid success outcome.

A-BALANCED-SPLIT-IMPLIES-RULE.statement: The roughly even split of disputed bills between ACTUAL and ESTIMATED read types (E-05) is interpreted as evidence of a read-type-agnostic billing import defect rather than two independent read-type-specific problems coincidentally overlapping.

A-SURGE-TIMING-ALIGNS-WITH-CAU.statement: The August onset of the dispute surge (E-03) is assumed to coincide with the onset of the billing rule defect, since no direct rule-change-log evidence has yet been reviewed to confirm the date.

A-FIELD-SHORTAGE-SECONDARY.statement: The field-reader staffing shortage described by SH-FIELD (E-07, stakeholder claim) is assumed to be a real but secondary contributor to the route completion shortfall (E-02), not the dominant driver of the dispute surge, given E-05.

structural_remedies.description: Deterministically query the billing-config DA-RULES change log for entries near Jul-Aug 2026 and compare timing to the surge onset (F-03) to confirm or reject H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is a read-only query on an authoritative data asset already in tool_surface (billing-config), with no AUTHORITY/HUMAN_APPROVAL constraint blocking reads; it directly resolves VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-EVIDENCE.; residual gap: billing-config tool_health is UNKNOWN (not yet confirmed HEALTHY), so the query may need retry; confirming the rule change does not itself correct already-issued wrong bills.

structural_remedies.description: If the log confirms a defective estimate-substitution/validation rule, correct the specific billing import validation rule in billing-config through Billing Operations' change-management process (configuration fix, not an agent).
structural_remedies.rationale: No AUTHORITY constraint explicitly covers billing-config writes (K-BILLWRITE only names write_bill_adjustment), so SH-BILL can authorize it, but safe rule-patch design, testing and rollout realistically exceed the 225-minute remaining budget.; residual gap: Still requires separate, non-automated billing adjustments (write_bill_adjustment under K-BILLWRITE) to correct bills already issued incorrectly.

structural_remedies.description: Formally designate SH-BILL as the sole approval authority for any write_bill_adjustment arising from the correction plan, closing the authority-owner gap flagged by the define_gate_result FAIL finding, per K-BILLWRITE.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is a pure governance/ownership clarification consistent with the existing K-BILLWRITE constraint and SH-BILL's authority_scope (billing_adjustments_manual); it requires no new tooling or time-intensive work.; residual gap: Does not fix the underlying billing-rule defect itself; only governs how any eventual bill corrections are executed.

structural_remedies.description: Address the secondary route-completion shortfall (E-02) by increasing ORG-FIELD contracted reader headcount per SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-07/CL-03), via contract amendment rather than an agent.
structural_remedies.rationale: Hiring/contracting additional field readers is a multi-week organizational change that cannot complete within the 225 remaining minutes, though no listed constraint blocks requesting it.; residual gap: E-05 shows disputes split near-evenly across ACTUAL and ESTIMATED read types, so fixing field staffing alone would not address the majority of disputes tied to ACTUAL reads.

structural_remedies.description: Pursue vendor provisioning of MDMS export access (currently HOLD/ACCESS_PENDING, seq 72) to unblock DA-MDMS review, as a vendor-contract/data-access fix rather than an agent task.
